Bye, Darling. No more @Charlotte Tilbury for the cruelty-free community.  THE TEA: Charlotte Tilbury has now publicly announced on their website they will not be renewing their Cruelty Free International certification.  THE BACKSTORY: Cruelty Free International (previously also referred to as The Leaping Bunny Programme) is the international coalition partner to Leaping Bunny (who certified North America). They recently announced a rebrand with a new logo. Both programs remain coalition partners with the same rigorous program, just certifying different regions.  THE WHY:  Allegedly, they are concerned about the public perception of this rebrand and its potential to cause confusion  THE ISSUE: 1. Charlotte Tilbury never has to print the rebranded logo on their packaging if they find the new logo from the previous bunny confusing. If they can write the giant chunk of text as their cruelty-free policy they recently revised, then they could have just as easily explained the rebrand and continued commitment.  2. Charlotte Tilbury now claims to be cruelty-free with zero audits, annual renewals, and is left unchecked selling on China where the brand could potentially begin selling their special use goods (which are subject to animal testing) in China. We are just expected to trust them.  3. Charlotte Tilbury is owned by parent company Puig with a large portfolio of other major brands all subject to animal testing as well. CT was the only cruelty-free brand in their collection. It makes this move extra questionable.
